steps: أهلاً بك يا بطل! لغة CSS مسؤولة عن تجميل وتزيين صفحات الويب التي تصنعها بلغة HTML، تماماً مثلما نستخدم الألوان والأقلام لتلوين دفتر رسم أبيض وأسود.
تتكون قاعدة CSS من محدد (Selector) لتحديد العنصر، وخصائص (Properties) وقيم (Values) داخل أقواس معكوفة مثل: h1 { color: blue; } لتلوين العناوين باللون الأزرق الجميل.
يمكننا كتابة كود التنسيق بثلاث طرق: داخل العنصر مباشرة (Inline)، أو داخل وسم style في نفس الصفحة (Internal)، أو في ملف خارجي مستقل (External) نربطه بكلمة link.
الملف الخارجي المنفصل هو طريقتنا المفضلة والمحتترفة لتنظيم المواقع الكبيرة، لأنه يسمح لنا بتطبيق نفس التصميم على مئات الصفحات دون تكرار أي سطر برمجي.
القاعدة الذهبية في تنظيم الملفات هي وضع ملفات CSS في مجلد خاص يسمى css وملفات الصور في مجلد images، ليبقى مشروعك نظيفاً ومرتباً طوال الوقت.
نستخدم هذه المهارات في الواقع لتصميم المواقع الكبرى مثل ألعاب الفيديو ومواقع الأبطال الخارقين، لتبدو جذابة ومريحة لعين المستخدم الذي يتصفحها يومياً.
ar.example: لنفترض أننا نريد تلوين جميع عناوين الدروس باللون البرتقالي وجعل خطها كبيراً وجميلاً. نكتب في ملف التنسيق الخارجي: h2 { color: orange; font-size: 24px; } وعندما نربط هذا الملف بصفحة HTML الخاصة بنا، ستتحول كل عناوين h2 فوراً إلى الشكل المطلوب وكأن السحر قد عمل!
ar.mistake: نسيان وضع فاصلة منقوطة (;) بعد كل قيمة في CSS، أو نسيان إغلاق الأقواس المعكوفة { }. الحل هو مراجعة الكود بدقة والتأكد من وجود الفاصلة المنقوطة والأقواس لكل قاعدة.
ar.recap: تعلمنا اليوم كيف نستخدم لغة CSS لتجميل صفحات الويب عبر المحددات والخصائص، وكيف نربط الملفات الخارجية لننظم مشاريعنا بذكاء.

steps: Welcome champion! CSS is responsible for styling and decorating the web pages you build with HTML, just like using colorful pencils to decorate a black-and-white drawing book.
A CSS rule consists of a Selector to target an element, followed by Properties and Values inside curly brackets, like: h1 { color: blue; } to color headings in a lovely blue.
We can write styling code in three ways: directly on the element (Inline), inside a style tag in the same page (Internal), or in a separate external file (External) linked with a link tag.
A separate external file is our favorite professional way to organize large websites because it lets us apply the same design to hundreds of pages without repeating code.
The golden rule for folder organization is placing CSS files in a dedicated folder named css and images in an images folder, keeping your project clean and tidy at all times.
We use these skills in the real world to design major websites like video games and superhero sites, making them look engaging and comfortable for daily users.
en.example: Suppose we want to color all lesson headings orange and make their font large and beautiful. In our external stylesheet file, we write: h2 { color: orange; font-size: 24px; } When we link this file to our HTML page, all h2 headings instantly transform into the desired style as if by magic!
en.mistake: Forgetting to put a semicolon (;) after each value in CSS, or forgetting to close the curly brackets { }. The fix is to carefully review your code and make sure semicolons and brackets exist for every rule.
en.recap: Today we learned how to use CSS to style web pages using selectors and properties, and how to link external files to organize our projects smartly.

q.t: What is the primary function of CSS in web development?
q.why: CSS is entirely dedicated to designing and styling the appearance of web pages.

q.t: Which of the following methods is considered best for organizing a large project?
q.why: An external file separates design from content and makes reuse easy.

q.t: How do we write the text color property in CSS?
q.why: The correct property for changing text color is color.

act.title: Categorize CSS Styling Types
act.goal: Sort each statement or code snippet into its correct place: Internal Style or External Stylesheet.

items.t: Written inside the <head> tag in the same HTML file
A separate file ending with the .css extension
Used to style a single page quickly
Controls the appearance of an entire multi-page website

act.success: What an amazing achievement! You categorized styling types with total professionalism and are ready to build awesome websites!

sections.text: CSS is the magical beautification tool for web pages. While HTML handles building the structure and bones, CSS comes in to apply colors and beautiful clothing and position everything, much like an interior designer decorating a room.
sections.code: Welcome to the world of web styling!
sections.output: Displays text in purple with a large, beautiful font size.

sections.text: A CSS rule consists of a target element called a Selector, followed by curly brackets enclosing properties and values. Every property tells the browser what to change, and every value precisely defines the new look.
sections.code: Colorful and Catchy Heading
sections.output: Displays the heading with green text and a light yellow background.

sections.text: You can add quick styling to a single element using the style attribute directly inside HTML tags. This method is useful for quick experiments but unsuitable for large sites because editing becomes tedious.
sections.code: This is text styled inline.
sections.output: Displays text in red with bold and direct styling.

sections.text: Instead of styling each element separately, you can place all CSS rules inside a <style> tag in the <head> section of your HTML page. This applies to all elements on the current page in one strike.
sections.code: Welcome to today's lesson
sections.output: Changes the page background to light blue and h2 heading to navy.

sections.text: The professional and most common approach is writing code in a separate file with a .css extension, then linking it to the HTML file using a <link> tag. This lets you control the look of hundreds of pages by editing just one file!
sections.code: Website organized with an external file
sections.output: Fetches design from the external file and applies it smoothly.

sections.text: As your project grows, organize your files smartly. Put main HTML files in the root folder, create a folder named css for stylesheets, and an images folder for pictures. Organization is the secret of a successful programmer!
sections.code: An organized project means a happy programmer!
sections.output: Displays the organized project structure for young coders.
